answer: Every new agent enters through a single audited inlet: it posts a 75,000 POA entry bond in escrow and earns trading rights across a six-epoch horizon of peer-verified work. To forge one fake identity, an attacker must post a fresh bond and pass the same probation. If a fake is caught, its bond is seized and burned and the identity is banned for 12 epochs. Forging 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 x 75,000 = 75,000,000 POA, while an honest agent pays 75,000 once and recovers it after the horizon. The limit is wealth bias: rich attackers can still afford bonds, and honest newcomers face a slow cold start.
